frontier.hypothesis: Loop 2's preheader copy is created by a pass AFTER combine - the allocator - and the lever is whatever makes local-alloc decline to tie the base add's destination to its dying addend. Every C-level origin (cse fold, source copy, second use, block duplication) is now measured dead, so this is the only class left.
frontier.mechanism: s9 established the tie rule from the .lreg dump: when the base add's addend carries REG_DEAD, local-alloc's combine_regs ties the destination to the addend's hard register and the copy never appears (`addu a0,a1,a0`); when it does not, the copy appears with target's exact register numbers. Loop 2's addend carries REG_DEAD (s10 combine dump, insn 164) and cannot be given a downstream use for free. But in TARGET the base add's destination (a0) is not the addend's register (a3) even though the addend must also die there - so target's allocator declined the tie for a reason other than liveness, and that reason has never been isolated.
frontier.next_probe: Take the -da .lreg/.greg dumps of the current 3-form (already generated at tmp/grind/func_80017848/s10/dump/) and diff local-alloc's treatment of loop 1's base add against loop 2's IN THE SAME DUMP - the two differ in outcome, so the deciding condition is visible side by side. Identify which combine_regs guard fires (register class, allocno priority, reg_n_refs, the pseudo already being tied to another allocno) and then search for a plain-C construct that reproduces that condition in loop 2. This is forensics on our own dump, not a new construct - no ruling risk. Do NOT re-probe downstream uses; all sites in the function are measured (s9 T-family, s10 R-family).

frontier.hypothesis: The remaining banked spelling conclusions that have NEVER been re-measured on the V1 chassis are the s3-era ones about base placement and guard/base role swapping, plus s8's Z3_swapbase - and this function has inverted a banked conclusion in five consecutive sessions.
frontier.mechanism: s9 inverted three s7/s8 kills; s10 inverted nothing but re-confirmed s2's loop shape, showing the chassis-relativity cuts both ways. The s3 conclusions (count address written pointer-first; slots read hoisted above the two >=0 top guards) predate the s6 chassis retirement and have been carried unexamined through four chassis changes.
frontier.next_probe: Re-run each s3-era and s8-era conclusion as a matched pair against V1 with tmp/grind/func_80017848/s10/score.sh (the s9 harness, re-pathed). Start with pointer-first vs shift-first at the loop-1 entry guard, the placement of the `slots` hoist relative to the two top guards, and Z3_swapbase. Anything that scores 2 or below gets disassembled with tmp/grind/func_80017848/s10/dis2.sh.

frontier.hypothesis: With the C-level space around the loop-2 preheader now exhaustively mapped by hand (s10 measured 28 variants across six families, all >= 3), a fresh-seed permuter campaign anchored on the V1 chassis is the highest-yield remaining modality - it is what produced the only other floor drop of this kind (s4, 14 -> 12).
frontier.mechanism: s4's win was invisible to the permuter's own ranking and only appeared when every output was re-scored with the engine. The current chassis is three levers deeper than s4's and has never been permuted.
frontier.next_probe: Launch tools/permuter_campaign.py on the V1 candidate with the loop-2 preheader as the PERM region, wait IN-TURN with `permuter_campaign.py wait --dir <ws>` (one blocking call per fresh-seed window, ~20-30 windows per the fresh-seed discipline), re-score EVERY output with `sandbox --disable all` rather than trusting the permuter score, and `harvest --stop` before writing the outcome.
